package_info.package_versions: versions vulnerable to CVE-2021-30116 (exact versions not specified in report)
package_info.why_malicious: The Kaseya VSA software was exploited via a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2021-30116) that allowed attackers to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary commands, enabling mass ransomware deployment to downstream endpoints managed by Kaseya and its MSP customers. The software itself was not maliciously modified, but its legitimate remote management features were abused for malicious purposes.

execution_context.trigger: remote exploit (pre-auth RCE) via zero-day vulnerability

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Arbitrary command execution via CVE-2021-30116 (details not disclosed in report, but involves unauthenticated attackers sending crafted requests to the VSA server to execute commands on managed endpoints).
malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (likely shell or PowerShell commands executed via VSA's scripting capabilities)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Allows attackers to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary commands on all endpoints managed by the compromised VSA server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unauthenticated remote command execution is a critical security risk, especially in remote management software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior: Only authenticated, authorized administrators can execute commands on endpoints. Malicious behavior: Attackers can execute commands without authentication.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be authenticated admins deploying scripts or updates to managed endpoints.
key_indicators: abuse of remote management scripting features

execution_context.file_location: deployed to all managed endpoints via VSA's scripting/payload deployment

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Ransomware payload (exact code not disclosed, but typically involves dropping and executing a ransomware binary on each endpoint, encrypting files, and displaying ransom note).
malicious_snippets.code_language: binary executable (likely Windows PE, could involve PowerShell or batch scripts for deployment)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Encrypts files on victim endpoints and demands ransom for decryption.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Mass deployment of ransomware to all managed endpoints is highly anomalous and destructive.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior: VSA used for legitimate software updates or scripts. Malicious behavior: Used to deploy ransomware to hundreds/thousands of endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be mass deployment of security patches or IT scripts.
key_indicators: simultaneous ransomware execution across many endpoints
use of IT management tool for malware delivery

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits zero-day (CVE-2021-30116) to gain unauthenticated remote code execution on Kaseya VSA server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to execute arbitrary commands on all managed endpoints.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses VSA's remote management features to deploy ransomware payload to all downstream endpoints.
attack_chain.leads_to: Mass ransomware infection and file encryption across customer networks.

behavioral_signatures: Unauthenticated remote command execution attempts against VSA server
Mass deployment of identical scripts or binaries to all managed endpoints in a short time window
Simultaneous ransomware activity across multiple endpoints managed by the same VSA instance
file_indicators: Unexpected scripts or binaries deployed via VSA's scripting or file distribution features
Presence of known ransomware binaries on endpoints
Ransom note files appearing on multiple endpoints simultaneously
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections from VSA server to attacker-controlled infrastructure
Spike in network traffic between VSA server and all managed endpoints
Possible C2 (command and control) traffic from endpoints post-infection
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for exploitation attempts against VSA's web interface, especially unauthenticated requests triggering command execution. Alert on mass deployment of new scripts or binaries via VSA, especially if not initiated by known administrators. Correlate simultaneous ransomware activity across endpoints managed by the same VSA instance. Monitor for known ransomware file indicators and ransom notes. Review VSA server logs for anomalous activity and privilege escalation.
